note: How fast the robot gets hungry, and how full it can get (pluggybot issue
#36). DATA, not code, on exactly the terms economy/rewards.json and
economy/cadence.json are: this is policy about a world, it wants re-tuning
against MEASURED throughput rather than against intuition, and a deploy has
to be able to change it on a mounted volume without a rebuild --
$PLUGGY_METABOLISM=/path/to/metabolism.json.
Points are FOOD. They are earned by working and consumed by living, and
once the robot has enough it is satisfied and spends its time on its own
goals instead. The whole mechanic is the free time; the numbers below are
what decides whether there is any.
READ THEM AGAINST MEASURED THROUGHPUT. Issue #36's arithmetic, off
economy/cadence.json's own note: a home charge-to-charge cycle is ~365
sim-seconds and one errand costs roughly one full pack, so the robot
finishes about one job per cycle -- ~10 jobs a sim-hour, at the 2-20 points
economy/rewards.json pays. That is a ~150 point/sim-hour ceiling and nearer
100 once offers lapse and jobs fail. A 100/hour appetite is therefore
SUBSISTENCE WITH NO FREE TIME, which deletes the point of the mechanic:
the rate has to leave the robot with hours it did not have to earn.
⚠ THESE ARE PROVISIONAL. They are issue #36's proposed starting point --
~45 points/hour against a ~90 cap, so roughly half the robot's capacity is
its own -- and NOT a measurement. Re-tune them here against a long run's
observed points/sim-hour, and re-tune them again whenever rewards.json or
cadence.json moves, because both of those change what an hour earns.
pointsPerHour  points consumed per SIM hour, charged a whole point at a
time (the fraction between carries in the ledger, so a
restart neither wipes hunger nor back-charges it)
cap            the most the balance may hold. Earnings past it are not
banked, and the ledger says how many were refused rather
than dropping them quietly
satisfiedAt    balance at which the robot has had enough and turns to its
own goals
hungryAt       balance at which it goes back to work. LOWER than
satisfiedAt on purpose: the gap is hysteresis, and without
it a robot sitting on the line flips state every point it
eats. The band is also the rhythm's period -- (satisfiedAt
- hungryAt) / pointsPerHour is how long the free time
lasts
A world block overrides the default block key by key, like cadence.json.
There are deliberately NO world blocks yet: room_hub and home earn at
different rates and nobody has measured either, and a per-world number
invented to look thorough is worse than one honest default.
